front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《12 》

en: A windless day
Fog, rendered in ink wash
Depicting the quiet of a tree
A cold night
A single lamplight
Concealing how many years of youthful rawness

points.zh:
去來江口守空船，繞舵明月江水寒。
夜深忽夢少年事，夢啼妝泪紅闌干。
我聞琵琶已嘆息，又聞此語重唧唧。
同是天涯淪落人，相逢何必曾相識。
--唐 。白居易《 琵琶行 》

en: Still pondering rhetoric and tone
Considering stacking and mood
When will this word game end
Tonight, the sky is full of starlight
Like scattered prayer beads
It is said the Buddha's law is boundless?

zh: 我留下一首未完成的詩給你
en: I leave you an unfinished poem
You left behind an open umbrella
For the endless spring rain
Now and then, remembering that moonlight
Then there is a clear breeze over the river
Fishing boats moor at shore, exchanging a word or two

points.zh: 「況吾與子，漁樵于江渚之上，侶魚蝦而友糜鹿，駕一葉之扁舟，舉匏樽以相屬﹔寄蜉蝣與天地，渺滄海之一粟。哀吾生之須臾，羨長江之無窮﹔挾飛仙以遨游，抱明月而長終﹔知不可乎驟得，托遺響于悲風。」 蘇子曰：「客亦知夫水與月乎？逝者如斯，而未嘗往也；盈虛者如彼，而卒莫消長也。蓋將自其變者而觀之，而天地曾不能以一瞬，自其不變者而觀之，則物于我皆無盡也。而又何羨乎？且夫天地之間，物各有主。苟非吾之所有，雖一毫而莫取。惟江上之清風，與山間之明月，耳得之而為聲，目遇之而成色。取之無禁，用之不竭。是造物者之無盡藏也，而吾與子之所共適。」     --宋。蘇東坡《前赤壁賦》
points.en:
"Moreover, you and I fish and gather firewood on the river's sandbars, keeping company with fish and shrimp, befriending deer; we ride a single leaf of a small boat, raising gourd cups to toast one another. We entrust our brief existence, like mayflies, to heaven and earth -- a single grain adrift in the vast sea. I lament the fleeting brevity of my life, and envy the endlessness of the great river. I long to soar with immortals in carefree wandering, to embrace the bright moon and last forever; knowing this cannot be suddenly attained, I entrust these lingering feelings to the mournful wind." Su Zi said: "Do you, my friend, understand the water and the moon? That which flows passes on like this, yet it has never truly gone; that which waxes and wanes does so like that, yet in the end there is no increase or decrease. If we view things from the perspective of change, then heaven and earth cannot last even the blink of an eye; but if we view things from the perspective of the unchanging, then all things, like ourselves, are inexhaustible. What then is there to envy? Moreover, between heaven and earth, each thing has its own master; if something is not truly mine to possess, I would not take even the smallest particle of it. Only the cool breeze over the river, and the bright moon between the mountains -- the ear catches them and they become sound, the eye meets them and they become color. Taking them incurs no prohibition, using them brings no depletion. These are the inexhaustible treasures of the Creator, and what you and I may enjoy together."
-- Su Dongpo (Song dynasty), "The Former Ode on the Red Cliff"

en: Snow drifts down softly
Saying, the beauty of quiet detachment
It is remembrance, and it is forgetting
The little stream flows with old stories
The reeds bend low
Picking up a few new words
Dusk fades into the distant mountains
Willow branches reflected in the pond
The hours spent grinding ink
The thick fog gradually clears
Listening quietly
The mood of one away from home

points.zh:
《 出外人 》    詞曲／蕭泰然
咱攏是出外人，對遠遠的臺灣來
雖然我會講美國話，話語會通心未通 
咱攏是出外人，在遠遠的臺灣彼
有咱的朋友與親人，不時互相在思念
蕭泰然（1938-2015）生於高雄鳳山，五歲由母親啟蒙，自小接受教會音樂和西洋古典音樂的薰陶，先後畢業於臺灣省立師範學院音樂專修科（今國立臺灣師範大學音樂系）、日本武藏野音樂大學鍵盤專攻科、加州州立大學洛杉磯分校音樂研究所，集教學、鋼琴家、指揮家、作曲家於一身。作曲以「台灣民謠的精神為主體，融入西方古典、浪漫、印象及現代音域的技巧，來培育現代的台灣新音樂。」被譽為「臺灣拉赫曼尼諾夫－最後的浪漫主義鋼琴詩人」。蕭泰然所創作的作品相當多元，以下為其部分主要作品。
協奏曲：「Ｄ調小提琴協奏曲」，「Ｃ調大提琴協奏曲作品五十二」，「Ｃ小調鋼琴協奏曲作品五十三」
管絃樂:「一九四七序曲」、「福爾摩沙交響曲」、「來自福爾摩沙的天使」
室內樂:「台灣原住民組曲」、「鋼琴三重奏《福爾摩沙》」
合唱曲:「玉山頌」、「台灣翠青」、「啊！福爾摩沙－為殉難者的鎮魂曲」
器樂曲：台灣頌、冥想曲、豐收（鋼琴四手聯彈）
蕭泰然來自富有文化教養的家庭，但其一生卻充滿困頓與顛沛，又飽受病痛之苦。然而，憑看堅定的信仰，以及對於台灣土地之愛，他從未屈服於現實環境，而是不斷地自我超越，燃燒生命，創造出無數詠頌上帝的聖樂、關懷台灣的作品；因此其作品格外打動人心，無須任何言語的解釋，自然就為他的音樂所感動。三度榮獲台灣金曲獎 ( 2004, 2010, 2011 ) ，2011年的金曲獎是傳統暨藝術音樂類「特別貢獻獎」。
《 出外人 》是1978年在亞特蘭大的作品， 一首深受旅外同鄉所喜愛的歌曲，將異鄉遊子的心情表露無遺，作曲者將其原來的獨唱曲，改編為合唱曲。由於歌詞和旋律的意境優美動人，不論是獨唱，合唱還是獨奏， 都能牽引離鄉遊子的情懷，以及心繫故土的思念。
林衡哲 編著，《深情的浪漫：蕭泰然音樂世界選輯》，1999年，台灣‧望春風出版杜
蔡明雲 著，《世界級的台灣音樂家：蕭泰然》，2006年，台灣‧玉山社
points.en:
《The One Away From Home》    Lyrics/Music: Tyzen Hsiao (Xiao Tairan)
We are all people away from home, coming from far-off Taiwan.
Although I can speak English, our words may connect but not our hearts.
We are all people away from home, over there in far-off Taiwan
are our friends and family, whom we constantly think of.
Tyzen Hsiao (1938-2015) was born in Fengshan, Kaohsiung. He began receiving music instruction from his mother at age five, and from childhood was immersed in church music and Western classical music. He successively graduated from the Music Program of Taiwan Provincial Normal College (now the Department of Music of National Taiwan Normal University), the Keyboard Program of Musashino Academia Musicae in Japan, and the Graduate School of Music at California State University, Los Angeles. He was at once a teacher, pianist, conductor, and composer. In his compositions, he took "the spirit of Taiwanese folk songs as the core, blending in the techniques of Western classical, romantic, impressionist, and modern music, to cultivate a modern new Taiwanese music." He was praised as "Taiwan's Rachmaninoff — the last Romantic poet of the piano." Tyzen Hsiao's works are quite diverse; below are some of his major works.
Concertos: "Violin Concerto in D Major," "Cello Concerto in C Major, Op. 52," "Piano Concerto in C Minor, Op. 53"
Orchestral works: "1947 Overture," "Formosa Symphony," "Angel from Formosa"
Chamber music: "Taiwan Aboriginal Suite," "Piano Trio 'Formosa'"
Choral works: "Ode to Jade Mountain," "Green Taiwan," "Ah! Formosa — Requiem for the Martyrs"
Instrumental works: Ode to Taiwan, Meditation, Harvest (piano four-hands)
Tyzen Hsiao came from a family of cultural refinement, yet his life was filled with hardship and displacement, and he suffered a great deal from illness. However, through steadfast faith and love for the land of Taiwan, he never yielded to circumstance, but continually surpassed himself, burning his life into countless sacred works in praise of God and works expressing concern for Taiwan; as a result, his works are especially moving, needing no explanation in words — one is naturally moved by his music. He won Taiwan's Golden Melody Award three times (2004, 2010, 2011); the 2011 Golden Melody Award was the "Special Contribution Award" in the traditional and art music category.
《The One Away From Home》 was composed in 1978 in Atlanta, a song deeply beloved by overseas compatriots, fully expressing the feelings of those far from home and their longing that remains tied to their native land. The composer later arranged his original solo piece into a choral work. Owing to the beautiful and moving imagery of its lyrics and melody, whether performed as a solo, choral piece, or instrumental piece, it stirs the sentiments of those who have left their hometown, and their longing for their native land.
Edited by Lin Hengzhe, 《Deep Romance: Selected Works from Tyzen Hsiao's Musical World》, 1999, Taiwan: Wangchunfeng Publishing House
Tsai Mingyun, 《A World-Class Taiwanese Musician: Tyzen Hsiao》, 2006, Taiwan: Yushan Publishing
